system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The LLM utilizes Claude Sonnet 4 and ChatGPT-4o with engineered prompts designed to synthesize mathematical expressions while maintaining formal correctness.
system_prompt_style.note: Prompts in Appendix A; system description is rendered per task.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: it performs feature-based retrieval using automatically extracted system attributes such as dimension, time domain, linearity, and topology. Candidate problems matching all features are shortlisted.
env_context_strategy.note: Retrieval is feature-based filtering plus LLM re-ranking over a database of prior solved systems, not lexical BM25; closest value chosen. No repository/file navigation.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: The Verifier Agent logs all intermediate results, enabling cumulative feedback that helps the Synthesis Agent learn from previous attempts.
context_compaction.note: No compaction mechanism described; history accumulates as cumulative feedback.

observation_format.evidence_quote: the Verifier Agent provides the violated conditions and counterexamples as feedback to the Synthesis Agent

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: engineered prompts designed to synthesize mathematical expressions while maintaining formal correctness
tool_call_format.note: Paper does not state a tool-call syntax; agents emit mathematical expressions parsed by the harness. Coded as closest value with low confidence.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: three collaborating agents: aBarrier Retrieval Agent, which searches a database of previously solved systems to identify analogous examples; aBarrier Synthesis Agent, which proposes candidate barrier certificates inspired by retrieved analogs; and aBarrier Verifier Agent
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing tool; agents produce mathematical expressions.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: it performs formal verification using SMT solvers such as Z3 (de Moura and Bjørner, 2008), Yices (Dutertre, 2014), and cvc5 (Barbosa et al., 2022)
protocol_standardization.note: Only direct SMT solver interfaces described; no MCP/A2A mentioned anywhere in the paper.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The pipeline consists of four stages: (1) historical retrieval, (2) LLM-based synthesis, (3) two-stage verification, and (4) iterative refinement guided by feedback.
loop_primitives.note: Verification failure feeds counterexamples back for refinement, bounded by K iterations and R refinements.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: LLMs guide the synthesis process by reasoning about system properties, safety requirements, and mathematical structure, first analyzing local safety conditions and then integrating them into global certificates.
planning_granularity.note: No stored plan object; the pipeline itself is fixed.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: our framework instantiates three collaborating agents: aBarrier Retrieval Agent, ... aBarrier Synthesis Agent, ... and aBarrier Verifier Agent
multi_agent_topology.note: Fixed hand-off retrieval -> synthesis -> verification with feedback loop back to synthesis.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Feedback from the Verifier Agent is returned to the Synthesis Agent, forming a closed-loop interaction bounded by a global timeout.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: The process terminates upon discovery of a valid barrier certificate or exhaustion of all attempts.
human_in_loop.note: Fully automatic loop; no human gating point described.

short_term_state.note: Algorithm maintains best candidate and score plus iteration/refinement counters beyond messages.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: A persistent database stores previously verified barrier certificates, which the Retrieval Agent accesses to accelerate synthesis on similar problems.
long_term_memory.note: RETRIEVALAGENT.STORE writes successful certificates back across runs.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: The process terminates upon discovery of a valid barrier certificate or exhaustion of all attempts.

self_verification.evidence_quote: In the first stage, it performs a sample-based validation across N points drawn from XI, XU , and X
self_verification.note: Second stage is SMT-based formal verification with Z3/Yices/cvc5.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: The system performs up to K main iterations, each exploring new template structures, and up to R refinements per iteration to adjust coefficients or terms.
retry_policy.note: Retries until the verifier passes, with caps K=5, R=4.

rollback.evidence_quote: If no valid certificate is found, the framework returns the candidate maximizing the proportion of satisfied conditions.
rollback.note: No filesystem or repo state to revert.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: forming a closed-loop interaction bounded by a global timeout
termination_condition.note: Also K/R iteration caps and termination on a verified certificate; a global timeout is stated too.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: We set maximum main iterations K= 5 and maximum refinements per iteration R= 4 .
cost_controls.note: Only iteration caps; no token budget, routing or caching described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: handles verification failures through solver switching or adaptive timeout adjustments
timeouts.note: Per-solver-call adaptive timeouts plus a stated global timeout on the closed loop.

permission_model.evidence_quote: then applies symbolic conversions or Taylor approximations when necessary, and handles verification failures through solver switching
permission_model.note: No authorization layer described; agent actions execute directly.

tracing.evidence_quote: The Verifier Agent logs all intermediate results, enabling cumulative feedback that helps the Synthesis Agent learn from previous attempts.

replayability.evidence_quote: The Verifier Agent logs all intermediate results, enabling cumulative feedback that helps the Synthesis Agent learn from previous attempts.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: By releasing BARRIERBENCHand the accompanying toolchain, we aim to establish acommunity testbedfor advancing the integration of language-based reasoning with formal verification
eval_hooks.note: Benchmark of 100 systems released with the framework toolchain; success measured by the built-in SMT verifier.

guardrails.evidence_quote: discarding invalid barriers that violate any of the three conditions on at least one of sampled points, to avoid unnecessary SMT solver calls
guardrails.note: Sample-based pre-check blocks invalid candidates from proceeding.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Safety verification of dynamical systems via barrier certificates is central to ensuring correctness in autonomous and other safety-critical applications.
target_domain.note: Domain is formal safety verification / control synthesis for cyber-physical systems.

open_source.note: Benchmark release stated; no licence or code repository cited in the paper.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: The LLM utilizes Claude Sonnet 4 and ChatGPT-4o with engineered prompts

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: we present anLLM-agentic framework for barrier certificate synthesisthat uses natural language reasoning to propose, refine, and validate candidate certificates.
primary_artifact.note: No code repository available for pinning.

first_release_date.note: Basis: arXiv id 2511.09363 implies v1 in November 2025; exact day inferred, low confidence.
